name: GUILDARMS-1-the-cache-never-read
note: The synchronous read skipping the cache: every read of a resolved tag starts a fetch, so a wagon's arms are re-asked every frame and the pool never settles on its upload key. The cache is the whole point of resolving by tag - without the read, resolution is a fetch per frame.

name: GUILDARMS-2-the-epoch-never-moved
note: The epoch never bumped on a resolution: the pool's upload key carries tag@epoch, so a tag that lands after the bare boards went up never rebuilds - every wagon keeps the bare boards it was first drawn with, and no error says the arms arrived.

name: GUILDARMS-3-the-fetch-never-started
old: const rows = Array.isArray(res?.body?.arms) ? res.body.arms : Array.isArray(res?.arms) ? res.arms : [];
note: The service answer thrown away unread: every tag resolves to no guild, so no wagon anywhere ever wears arms - and the fetch still ran, so nothing about the failure is visible except wagons with no heraldry on them.

name: GUILDARMS-4-the-seed-never-kept
note: Seeding the owner's own tag keeping nothing: the reader's own wagon - the one case that should never need the wire - resolves through a fetch like a stranger's, or not at all offline.
